originalText:
Fable 5 / Mythos brought the magic back for me holy shit 👽

give this monster a /goal and it will blow your mind

i know i know, just UI stuff, but i was terrified of this mission lol as the dashboard was getting complex and thought this would be a solid thing to point it at

my current workflow is usually to build well researched imp plans w/ a lot of back and forth, i was dreading it for this task... 

said fuck it and just gave it a one prompt goal...

26 commits later and it's nailed it (I only stepped in a few times here there w/ observations, taste related stuff).

A couple observations: 

Fable is amazing at surfacing bugs mid-flight: take advantage of this, wire it into the initial prompt or goal w/something like 'continuously sweep for bugs and log them in a file, we'll discuss post mission' or just 'YOLO fix any bug you find'

Give it clear constraints and clarity on what 'done' looks like. I could have done better at this. 

Let Fable COOK, don't try and steer it too hard. Give it a couple skills maybe, that's it. 

Enjoy the Fable BBQ cookout. I am maxing this shit out until the 22nd.

title: Fable 5 benchmark results compared with other models
author: Ninza
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
A user on Reddit shared a MineBench comparison between Claude Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, and the results are honestly pretty interesting.

Fable 5 averaged ~18 mins inference time, while Opus 4.8 took almost ~25 mins on average.

Which is funny because on Claude, Fable actually feels slower and like it thinks forever 

The cost numbers were interesting too:
Fable 5 → $54.93 for 15 builds
Opus 4.8 → $41.52 for 15 builds

And this is despite Fable’s API pricing being 2x more expensive than Opus 4.8.

So the benchmark creator thinks Fable is probably generating way fewer tokens overall, which is helping keep the cost relatively lower.

What’s also interesting is that the builds apparently weren’t some gigantic leap over GPT 5.5 Pro visually, but Fable showed insane attention to tiny details.

One example was a Pac-Man arcade build where it correctly added the game screen, score counter, and even the “1UP” label

Also apparently adding prompts like:
“LEVEL OF DETAIL: MAXIMUM”
“BOUNDING BOX: UNLIMITED”

improved the outputs a lot.

Benchmarks are slowly becoming half model eval and half prompting skill issue at this point.
summary: Shares updated coding-agent benchmark results and positions Claude Fable 5 against other frontier coding agents.

title: Landing page generated with Fable 5
author: Sourasith
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Claude Fable 5 is a beast at creating full landing pages with a complete on-scroll experience from just one prompt 😱 

Since this new model just came out and is more expensive, I didn’t want to waste credits testing random prompts, so I planned everything carefully before using it.

On-scroll experience has always been one of my weaknesses, and I’ve been trying to understand how to make it better. I think I finally found a workflow that works for me.

I picked a website for inspiration, recorded the full landing page while scrolling, and used Codex to analyze the website and the video. It created screenshots, broke down the on-scroll experience, and helped me write a very detailed prompt to recreate the same type of motion, but with a completely different brand, color palette, text, and visual direction.

Then I gave that prompt to Claude Fable 5, attached the full landing page screenshots, and asked it to build the whole landing page in one shot.

The result is honestly crazy. It created pinned scroll sections, oversized typography, floating 3D cards, expanding gallery grids, product mockups, a profile builder, a community board, and even an on-load animation.

I’m currently recording this full workflow to teach you how I planned the prompt, analyzed the reference website, broke down the on-scroll experience, and used Claude Fable 5 to build the landing page in one shot.

title: Fable 5 benchmark results compared with other models
author: West Lord
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
ChatGPT built Minecraft in 6 hours. Claude Fable 5 gets 1 shot to beat it.

Anthropic dropped Fable 5 this week and the glaze went nuclear. So 1 dev rigged a fight: 2 models, 1 task build Minecraft from scratch, in the browser, no game engine.

The rules weren’t fair. On purpose.

ChatGPT got reference images of the game. Unlimited retries.

Fable 5 gets 0 images. 1 attempt. No mercy.

ChatGPT went first. 6 hours of compute. 2,110 lines of code.

He opened the file expecting garbage.

Day/night cycle. A working inventory with textured blocks. Trees you can break and place. Transparent water you can mine the thing real Minecraft never let you do. F3 pulls up a live FPS counter and XYZ coordinates.

It looked like the 2010 alpha build. Running on a potato PC. $0 in dev salaries.

Microsoft paid $2.5B for this game. A prompt rebuilt it before dinner.

And here’s the bait on the hook: that was the weaker model’s run.

Fable 5 the one topping every benchmark, the one fighting blindfolded with 1 shot hasn’t even started.

One model already shipped a game. The favorite hasn’t typed a line.

originalText:
Everyone's posting about Claude Fable 5. 

I'm chasing the shiny object my own way: from now on, every app I need, I vibe code on demand. 

Need Discord to game with my friends? Ship it. 
Need Adobe Audition to edit down some audio? Ship it. 
Need VLC media player to convert a video file? Ship it.

No downloads. No subscriptions. No ToS. No privacy breaches. Just me and Claude, building my digital nest. 

I dub this movement the coding cottage industry.

title: 「AI開発に一斉ブレーキを」と世界に訴えた翌週、Anthropicが最強モデル「Claude Fable」を...
author: AI×Businessの研究｜Eiko.Hiyama
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
「AI開発に一斉ブレーキを」と世界に訴えた翌週、Anthropicが最強モデル「Claude Fable」を投入。出力100万トークンあたり$50という値付けの中身を、技術系チャンネルFireshipが検証しています。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

【"Mythosクラス"の最強モデル、ただし期間限定公開】
動画では、Claude Fableは内部開発の「Mythos 5」と同じ土台で、安全のための分類器モデルを被せた版だと説明されています。価格は出力100万トークンあたり$50（Opusの$25の2倍）。有料Claudeプランなら6/22まで使え、その後はトークン課金のみ——「FOMOを煽る巧みな施策」と評されています。

【ガードレールは"蒸留対策"でもある】
サイバーセキュリティ・生物・化学・モデル蒸留に関わる質問は、分類器が検知してClaude Opus 4.8の回答に差し替えられる構造だと紹介。結果として、DeepSeekやKimiといった中国勢が同等のオープンソース版をすぐ作るのは難しい、という見立てが語られています。

【エンジニアの初期評価は上々】
GPU向け言語「Bend」の作者が、Fableが自分のコードを大幅に高速化したことを「自分にとっての特異点の瞬間」と称賛。動画主自身もUI生成を試し、崩れがちなSVG（ベクター画像）をきれいに描く点や、Tinder風スワイプアニメの再現度に驚いたとレポートしています。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

「ブレーキを」と訴えた直後に最強モデル——この矛盾をどう読むか。煽り口調の動画ながら、価格・制約・実力の要点はしっかり押さえた一本です。

#Claude #ClaudeFable #生成AI #Anthropic #AI
